chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
'There is no goodness in life except for two men — a scholar who is obeyed, or an attentive listener.'

key_terms.الْعَيْشُ: Life/living — the span of one's existence in this world
key_terms.عَالِمٍ مُطَاعٍ: A scholar who is obeyed — one whose knowledge translates into guidance that others follow
key_terms.مُسْتَمِعٍ وَاعٍ: An attentive/retaining listener — one who does not merely hear but preserves and acts on knowledge

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the value of life and the two types of people worth living for?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from the Prophet (SAWW), presents a striking assessment: that life holds no real value or benefit except for two types of people — the scholar whose knowledge is acted upon, and the sincere listener who internalizes what they hear. The pairing highlights that knowledge is only beneficial when it produces both qualified teachers and receptive students. In the early Islamic community, this teaching served as a call to take learning seriously and to ensure that religious knowledge would be properly transmitted and applied.
